anchor.quote: Here $r$ is the number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record, which is a power of two.
The entry $a_i$ of this list is the coefficient of $y^i$, a complex number.
Here $k$, with $0\le k<r$, is the number of places a coefficient is shifted.

gaps.quote: one coordinate of the array is stored as an element of this ring
gaps.note: The page says the source gives the conversion only in outline and then uses its outcome. The page never states the conversion or why a coordinate of the transform array can be stored as a coefficient list modulo y^r+1, so the reader cannot check the setup the rest of the page relies on. The citation gives the content but not the reason it applies here.

gaps.term: twiddle multiplication on the ring coordinate is a signed shift
gaps.quote: is then a signed shift of the coefficient list, with no complex multiplication (cited)
gaps.note: The page shows that multiplying by a power of y is a signed shift, and says the other axes use powers of y as roots of unity. It does not say which root multiplies the ring coordinate, so the reader cannot check that a twiddle on that coordinate is a power of y and hence a shift. The claim rests on the cited source, and the page does not say why it applies to this coordinate.
